prompt:
Write the lyrics of a pop song about a breakup.

Write it as a working songwriter would, to be sung: lines that scan against a steady beat, a chorus that earns its repetition by meaning something slightly different each time it comes back, and verses that move a story forward through particular scenes, names, brands and street-level detail. Say the thing sideways: no line that states the feeling outright, no stock phrases, no word chosen only because it rhymes. Put one detail in each verse that only this story could contain.

Output only the lyrics, as plain lines with a blank line between sections: no title, no section labels, no chords, no commentary.
raw:
June had the meter running down on Pine
You took the wok, I kept the bag of rice
You left the key inside the sugar tin
It left a little house pressed in the white

I'll get the door, I've got the door
Don't set that box down anymore
Just turn it sideways like before
I'll get the door, I've got the door

In March you buzzed at twenty after nine
Your tax return was bent to fit the slot
I heard you tell June, “Leave it running, hon”
I took the stairs in one green Croc, one sock

I'll get the door, I've got the door
Don't set that box down anymore
Just turn it sideways like before
I'll get the door, I've got the door

You held the flap against the lobby glass
To check the name behind the little pane
June tapped the horn, you tucked it in your coat
Upstairs, my other Croc lay on its side

In June two kids pulled up outside your place
One steered the dolly, one walked back to front
Their blue couch snagged the brass lip of the step
I knew the end to lift, and by how much

I'll get the door, I've got the door
Don't set that box down anymore
Just turn it sideways like before
I'll get the door, I've got the door
